related issue: #57398

pr_comments: All my above review comments seem to relate to pre-existing code which is just being moved around, so it shouldn't be blocking for this PR. But a follow-up PR cleaning the code in this class following my comments would be great :)

issue_context.title: (4.0) Can't edit font size on multiple objects at once
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0 alpha 1

### System information

Windows 11

### Issue description

This is not so much bug but kinda lack of cohesion. For example if i select multiple Label nodes I can modify they modulation and other properties. Simply make change on X nodes at a time.

But if I pick multiple labels. New font menu at the top dissapear and if I want to change font size I need to do it one by one.

One Label:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/62170071/151660870-16bc14c5-a678-43e6-9f22-6212b49a03cb.png)

Multiple Labels:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/62170071/151660888-15be070e-098d-4a02-8ac5-3cae5ca17d04.png)


### Steps to reproduce

Simply select multiple Labels.

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments: I'm trying to deal with it. However, there is a question I need to figure out. If I select two labels with different properties (different font sizes e.g.), which value should be displayed in the editor? Or do I need to add another value (like `--` in some editor) to show that these two labels' font sizes are different?

I think the Photoshop approach is kinda good in this situation. In Photoshop if you select multiple text layers font size is just not displayed. So leaving empty space in font-size property or adding ```--``` as you said is a good idea in my opinion.

Word (Microsoft software in general) is doing it same way as Photoshop. Leaving empty space. So it is kinda standard.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/62170071/152637033-a3333c1b-3619-4c05-8243-32c5a1f8e01f.png)

review_comments: To be confirmed, but I think these could be changed to be wrapped with `SNAME()` (and defined as `StringName` instead of `String`) to reuse preallocated StringNames for performance.

```suggestion
					ur->add_do_method(edited_control, SNAME("add_theme_font_override"), edited_font, font);
```
etc. for other string literals passed when `StringName` is expected.

It's better to cast instead of relying on strings:
```suggestion
			if (Object::cast_to<RichTextLabel>(edited_control)) {
```
This (and line 225) can wrap the string literal in `SNAME` to get a statically allocated StringName instead of an implicit coercion.
